rv.q: The painting forms the matrix of Rockets and Blue Lights, Pinnock’s inspirationally ambitious and all-encompassingly humane examination of the unresolved history of the transatlantic slave trade.
The script is sometimes let down by casual plotting and cliched dialogue.
The wealth of overlapping stories give the drama an exciting, anarchic edge but also create cerebral circles within circles.
'Rockets and Blue Lights' is illuminated by dazzling flashes of brilliance. But ... I could never quite grasp the full shape of what Pinnock and Crowell were creating.
The play is a sprawling piece of work, and the pacing is oddly modulated, with a first half that takes its time setting up its chess pieces, and a second that lands only some of its gut-punches.
In effect, there are three or four playlets competing for our attention, and none of them comes to life.
I respected the gesture more than I admired the art, and while I cannot argue with the integrity of her vision, I can protest that she has crammed too much into too little space.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this ambitious but overstuffed drama, with critics praising moments of brilliance and strong performances while faulting sprawling structure, uneven pacing, and tangled plotting that obscures the play's vision.
